clips.text: After school, Ben sits on a chair at his desk.
He opens his workbook to do his homework.
One math question is hard, so Ben thinks carefully.
Ben looks at his dad and asks, “Can you help me?”
Dad smiles warmly and says, “Let me see.”
Dad helps him step by step, and Ben happily says, “I am finished.”
Dad gives him a high five and says, “Good job!”
Roommates Leah and Sam set a weekly budget of one hundred and twenty dollars for shared groceries and cleaning supplies.
“I would rather buy less meat than cut back on fresh vegetables,” Leah says.
Sam agrees, but asks, “Does that include a reserve for unexpected costs?”
They allow eighty dollars for groceries and twenty-five for supplies, leaving fifteen as a buffer.
“We can split the total equally, provided that personal snacks come from our own money,” Sam suggests.
Leah agrees to contribute sixty dollars, but adds, “Any spending above the weekly limit needs both of us to agree first.”
Sam agrees to contribute the same amount and says, “The trade-off is less variety, but we can keep our spending under control.”
They will review the plan after two weeks and discuss any changes before raising the limit.
After class, Kevin stays in the classroom to talk to his English teacher.
He looks at the helpful feedback written on his essay.
Kevin points to a note and asks, “Could you explain this part?”
He wants to do better and asks, “How can I improve my writing?”
The teacher gives him clear advice on organizing his main ideas.
Kevin smiles and says, “Thank you for the advice.”
The teacher smiles back and encourages him, “Keep up the good work.”
Today, Leo goes to Sam's home for a fun birthday party.
All the friends smile warmly and cheer, “Happy birthday!”
Leo gives Sam a wrapped gift and says, “This gift is for you.”
They gather around the table and sing a happy birthday song together.
Mom brings out a sweet cake with a glowing candle on top.
Everyone shouts, “Make a wish!” and Sam blows out the candle.
Sam smiles at his friends and says, “Thank you for coming.”
On a sunny morning, Ethan waits by the bus stop with his backpack.
He checks the bus number and says happily, “Here comes the bus.”
To be sure, he asks a student next to him, “Does this bus go to our school?”
The student smiles and answers, “Yes, it does! Tap your card.”
Ethan steps onto the bus and taps his card against the reader.
He walks down the aisle, and a friendly passenger says, “Have a seat.”
Ethan sits down with a smile and enjoys the ride to school.
On a sunny morning, Mia stops at a small café.
She looks at the menu and says, “I'd like a coffee and some toast, please.”
The barista asks, “For here or to go?”
“To go, please,” Mia says.
The barista puts her toast in a paper bag.
“How much is it?” Mia asks at the counter.
“Five dollars,” the barista says.
Mia pays, takes her breakfast, and says, “Thank you!”
Before choosing a place for the book swap, Ben shows Maya a screenshot saying the library is closed.
“Let's check the source first,” Maya says, rather than forwarding the warning.
They open the original notice on the school website, and Maya asks, “Is it still up to date?”
“It was posted last year, during the repairs,” Ben says.
“That doesn't necessarily mean it's closed now,” Maya replies.
A current notice says the library meeting room is available on Friday, although the reading area must stay quiet.
“We should confirm the details,” Ben says, and the librarian tells them the room can hold twenty people.
They save the link and date so everyone in their group can check the information for themselves.
Emily and Brian review every elective course offered for next semester.
Unsure about his academic plan, Brian sighs and asks, “Which course should I choose?”
Emily compares an advanced physics class with a world literature seminar to check how much academic credit each offers.
Brian points to the artificial intelligence syllabus, explaining his deep interest in data science: “I'm interested in this course.”
Emily smiles and cautions him about the heavy lab workload, adding, “That sounds challenging.”
After checking his weekly timetable to avoid time conflicts, Brian says happily, “It fits my schedule.”
He clicks the registration button with confidence, eager to learn new skills.
Leo looks at his desk, but he only has an eraser and a ruler.
He forgot his pencil and turns to his classmate Mia for help.
Leo asks politely, “Can I borrow a pencil?”
Mia smiles warmly and says, “Here you are.”
Leo takes the pencil and says, “Thank you very much.”
Mia answers with a friendly smile, “You're welcome.”
Their teacher smiles at them and starts the lesson.
During the school club fair, Kevin walks over to the science club booth.
Curious about their projects, he smiles and asks, “What do you do here?”
A friendly member replies, “We build models and plan a fun activity every week.”
Kevin is interested in the schedule and asks, “When do you meet?”
“We meet every Thursday after class in the lab,” the student explains.
Kevin is very excited and says, “I'd like to join the club.”
Then he asks, “Where can I sign up?” and takes a pen to sign his name.
Mia and Leo sit together at a big table in art class.
The teacher smiles and reminds everyone, “Be careful with scissors.”
Mia cuts a bright sheet of paper and says, “What a pretty color!”
Leo wants to paste paper shapes and asks, “Pass me the glue, please.”
Mia hands him the glue with a friendly smile.
Leo holds up his paper lion and cheers, “Look at my craft!”
At the front gate, Emily greets Mark, a foreign exchange student from Seattle.
With a bright smile, she waves her hand and says, “Welcome to our school!”
Emily enthusiastically offers, “Let me show you around.”
She will guide him to explore each modern campus facility, starting with the main academic building.
Pointing toward a spacious hall, she says, “Here is the library.”
Next, she highlights the cafeteria nearby, where students gather for lunch and relax between classes.
Offering her full support, Emily smiles and adds, “Feel free to ask me anything.”
On Saturday morning, Ben and his mom sit at the kitchen table.
Mom looks up from the table and says, “Let's check the fridge.”
Ben opens the door, looks inside, and asks, “Do we need any eggs?”
Mom looks at the empty egg carton and says, “Yes, and we also need fresh milk.”
Ben holds the pencil ready, and Mom says, “Write it on the list.”
With their shopping items written down for the market, Mom smiles and says, “We are ready to go.”
On Friday evening, Dad sits down with the family and smiles, “Let's plan our trip.”
Mom opens a notebook and suggests visiting a scenic mountain park this weekend.
Dad checks his phone and says the weather will be sunny and clear.
Emily raises her hand excitedly and asks, “What should we bring?”
Mom smiles and reminds everyone, “Don't forget your hat.”
They also decide to pack sandwiches and water for a pleasant picnic.
Looking forward to the hike, everyone cheers, “It will be so much fun!”
Alex visits the guidance counselor's office to discuss which university subject best matches his strengths.
Ms. Lin smiles warmly, points to an exploratory chart, and asks, “What are your interests?”
Alex explains his deep interest in technology and design, adding, “I'd like to learn more about interactive media.”
Ms. Lin suggests combining both fields into an interdisciplinary college major.
Looking over the degree pathways together, she encourages him, “Consider your future career.”
Alex organizes his ideas into a clear study plan and smiles, “Thank you for the advice.”
At a planning meeting, Maya presents a proposal for a book swap that thirty students will attend.
“We recommend using the library meeting room because it will keep the books dry.”
“According to the current notice, the room is available on Friday.”
“The main advantage is that we won't need to cancel if it rains.”
Ben adds, “However, there's a limit of twenty people, so we suggest two sessions of fifteen.”
A classmate asks how they will keep the reading area quiet.
“We could close the meeting-room door and ask everyone to keep their voices down,” Maya replies.
“Our next step is to ask the librarian to reserve the room,” Maya says, and the group agrees.
After school, Leo has a question about today's English assignment and walks over to his classmate Mia.
He opens his pencil case and asks, “When is the homework due?”
Mia checks her study planner and says, “It is due this Friday morning before the bell rings.”
Leo flips open his workbook and asks, “Which page is it?”
Mia points to the reading section and answers, “We need to complete page thirty-four.”
Leo writes down the notes with a smile and says, “Thanks for your help.”
Mia packs her backpack and replies cheerfully, “No problem at all.”
Toby walks into the neighborhood library with his mother.
A sign on the wall says, “Please be quiet in the library.”
He looks at the tall shelf to find a fun story.
He finds a picture book about animals that he wants to read.
Toby walks to the librarian and asks, “Can I borrow this book?”
He smiles and says, “Here is my library card.”
The librarian stamps the book and says, “Enjoy your reading!”
Leo walks into the classroom after PE class.
He checks his desk, but he cannot find his water bottle.
Leo asks his teacher and friends, “Have you seen my water bottle?”
His teacher smiles and asks, “Where did you leave it?”
Leo thinks for a moment and says, “It is blue and small.”
They go back to the playground, and his friend points to a bench.
Leo runs over and cheers, “Here it is!”
Leo walks into the cafeteria and asks, “What's for lunch?”
He sees hot chicken and says, “It looks delicious.”
Leo says to the cook, “I'd like some rice, please.”
He chooses a fresh vegetable and asks, “Can I have some soup?”
The cook smiles and puts the warm food on his tray.
Leo sits with his friends and happily enjoys his lunch.
During lunch break, Leo sits on a courtyard bench and starts a conversation with a new friend named Sam.
Curious about Sam's interests, Leo turns to him and asks, “What do you like to do?”
Sam points to his instrument case and replies, “I love playing guitar.”
Leo's eyes light up with excitement as he replies, “Me too!”
They quickly realize that music is their shared hobby and discuss the songs they listen to after school.
Before the bell rings, they gladly exchange contact information, and Sam says, “Let's hang out sometime.”
The morning sun shines brightly into the room.
Mom comes in with a warm smile and says, “Good morning!”
She gently taps Leo and says, “It's time to get up.”
Leo wakes up happily and brushes his teeth.
Next, he sits down at the table to eat breakfast.
Mom points to the hallway and says, “Put on your shoes.”
Leo opens the front door to go to school and calls, “See you later!”
Today, our class arrives at the history museum for an exciting field trip.
A friendly museum guide welcomes our group at the entrance and gives us maps.
Before we explore the galleries, Mr. Chen reminds us, “Take some notes.”
Inside the ancient hall, Leo points to a glass case and whispers, “Look at this exhibit.”
We admire a rare gold bowl from thousands of years ago and write down facts about it.
As lunchtime approaches, Emily raises her hand and asks, “Where should we meet?”
Mr. Chen smiles and announces, “By the main gate at noon. Don't be late.”
Leo gets ready for school the next day.
Mom comes into the room and asks, “Are you ready?”
Leo checks his items and asks, “Where is my notebook?”
Mom finds it beside an English book and says, “Here it is!”
She hands it to Leo with a smile and says, “Put it in the bag.”
Leo finds his ruler, then puts his pencil and notebook inside the schoolbag.
Everything is ready, so he zips up the schoolbag.
Leo goes outside to play with his pet dog in the yard.
Mom pours fresh water into a clean bowl and says, “Let's give the dog some water.”
Next, Leo fills the food bowl and calls, “Time to eat!”
After eating, Leo gently brushes Toby's fur and smiles, “Good boy!”
Then, Leo throws a red ball across the grass and shouts, “Fetch the ball.”
Toby happily brings the ball back to Leo's hands.
The children have fun together on the playground.
Amy swings high on the swing, and Leo walks to the big slide.
Leo smiles at Mia and asks, “Can I play too?”
Mia nods and says, “Yes! Let's wait in line.”
Leo waits patiently and asks, “Is it my turn?”
Mia smiles and says, “It's your turn now.”
Leo slides down the slide, and the children are happy to play together.
Owen calls a pottery studio to move a booking for two people from Saturday to Sunday.
“Could we move our session to the afternoon?” he asks.
The receptionist says the afternoon is full, but two places are available at ten in the morning.
“If there is no extra charge, we could take the morning session,” Owen replies.
“The price stays the same, but any change depends on availability when you call back before five today,” she explains.
“Could you keep the original booking until then?” he asks, because his friend has not agreed yet.
She agrees to keep Saturday booked but warns that the Sunday places cannot be held without confirmation.
Owen will check with his friend and call back before five, knowing that Sunday may no longer be available.
After school, Leo sits on a wooden bench to talk openly with his friend Ethan.
They had an awkward misunderstanding because of a confusing text message sent yesterday.
Leo shows his phone and explains that he did not mean to sound rude, saying, “That's not what I meant.”
He looks at Ethan sincerely and adds, “I am sorry about that.”
Ethan takes a deep breath and is willing to listen carefully to his explanation.
Understanding the whole situation, Ethan smiles and says, “Thanks for explaining.”
They bump fists happily on the bench, and Leo says, “We are still friends.”
Maya and Ben are choosing a location for a Friday book swap with thirty students.
Ben points to the school courtyard and says, “We could hold it here because there's plenty of space.”
“I see your point, but the forecast says it might rain,” Maya replies.
“My main concern is keeping the books dry.”
Ben suggests the library instead, although he is not sure whether it is available.
“Let's compare the options before we decide,” Maya says.
Ben agrees: “That sounds reasonable, as long as we check how much space we can use.”
They write down their shared goal: a place with enough room and protection from the rain.
Noah brings a pair of faulty headphones and his receipt to the store.
“The sound cuts out on the left side,” he explains to the assistant.
“Could you clarify when it happens?” she asks before testing them.
Noah replies, “It happens even when the battery is full.”
The assistant finds the same problem and offers a replacement.
“Would a refund be possible?” Noah asks, because he has already bought another pair.
“I need approval from my manager,” she says, “so I cannot promise a refund yet.”
“Just to confirm, you will check with your manager before I decide,” Noah says.
While walking inside the community center, Kevin notices a lost leather wallet on the floor near the entrance.
He picks up the lost item and decides to return it right away.
Kevin walks across the lobby to the information desk to report what he discovered.
Approaching the counter, he tells the attendant, “I found this wallet near the door.”
The staff member smiles warmly and asks, “Where did you find it?”
After Kevin explains what happened, the officer says, “Thank you for bringing it here.”
She safely stores the item in a drawer and adds, “Someone will be very relieved.”
Today, every student is excited because our school is holding its annual festival.
Our class sets up a colorful booth to sell handmade cookies and fun games.
When visitors walk by, Mia waves happily and calls out, “Welcome to our booth!”
A friendly customer stops at our table to look around.
Leo points to our fresh treats and asks, “Would you like to try one?”
The customer smiles and says, “One ticket, please.”
After handing over the snack, the students wave and say, “Thanks for coming!”
It is the first day of school, and Leo walks into the classroom.
A friendly girl smiles and says, “Hello!”
Leo smiles back and says, “Hi, my name is Leo.”
Then he asks, “What is your name?”
The girl says, “Nice to meet you! I am Emma.”
Leo says, “Nice to meet you, too. Let's be friends!”
During the break, Kevin walks into the school store.
He is hungry and asks the clerk, “Can I get a snack?”
After choosing a bun, Kevin asks, “Where are the drinks?”
He finds a cold bottle in the fridge and asks, “How much is this juice?”
“The price is thirty dollars,” the clerk answers with a smile.
Kevin hands her a fifty-dollar coin and says, “Keep the change.”
The clerk laughs, gives him twenty dollars, and says, “Take your change and enjoy your snack!”
As classes end, Kevin packs his bag and asks Mia, “What time does practice start?”
Mia ties her sneakers and says, “It starts at four o'clock. See you on the field.”
Soon, the whole soccer team gathers on the sports field around their coach.
The coach blows his whistle and explains the drill for Friday's big game.
During drills, Kevin receives the ball and makes a crisp pass to his teammate.
“Nice pass!” shouts Mia as she kicks the soccer ball into the net.
Before heading home, the players gather in a circle and say, “Let's do our best.”
Leo stops on a neighborhood street and checks his phone.
He asks a woman, “How do I get to the station?”
“Go straight along this street,” she says, pointing ahead.
“Then turn left at the traffic light.”
“The station is next to the bank.”
“It's about a five-minute walk from here.”
“Thank you for your help,” Leo says.
He puts away his phone and starts walking.
After school, three high school classmates gather in the library to organize their weekly study group.
As they open their biology textbooks, Emily suggests, “Let's review this chapter first.”
Looking over the upcoming exam requirements, David turns to the team and asks, “What is your main goal?”
Next, they discuss how to divide each presentation topic for their class report.
Pointing at the diagram on genetics, Hannah volunteers, “I can cover this section.”
After finalizing an efficient study schedule, David smiles and says, “Let's take a short break.”
Nora takes a basket at the supermarket.
She asks a staff member, “Where can I find the milk?”
“It's in aisle three,” the staff member says.
She walks with Nora to aisle three and points to the milk on a shelf.
“I'll take a carton of milk,” Nora says, putting it in her basket.
She picks up some bread and apples, too.
At checkout, she asks, “Can I pay by card?”
She pays by card and puts everything in a bag.
After class, our group gathers around a library table to work on an English project.
Kevin opens his notebook and asks, “What should we do first?”
Mia shares a creative idea about world festivals.
Leo agrees and says, “That's a great idea.”
Next, we divide each task, and Mia offers to do the research.
Leo smiles and says, “I can make the poster.”
Before packing up, Kevin says, “Let's meet on Friday.”
Leo looks around his bedroom and says, “Look at this mess.”
Many blocks and toy cars are all over the floor.
Mom smiles and says, “Let's put the toys away.”
Leo picks up a toy car, and Mom says, “Put it in the box.”
They put every toy into the box and make the bed.
Leo looks at his tidy room and smiles, “Now it is clean.”
Leo and his friend Mia sit on the carpet in the living room.
Leo smiles and says, “Let's play together.”
Mia looks at the colorful box and asks, “Can I share your toy?”
Leo hands her a red engine and says, “Here is a train.”
Mia places a wooden block on the rug to build a bridge.
Together, they connect the pieces and cheer, “We built a track!”
The two friends watch the little cars roll and have fun all afternoon.
Leo and his mother enter the busy train station with their luggage.
They look up at the large departure board to check the train schedule.
Leo shows their ticket to a station employee and asks, “Which platform should we go to?”
The employee checks the ticket and says, “Your train to Taipei is at platform two.”
Leo looks around the busy station and asks, “Where is platform two?”
The employee points toward the stairs and says, “Here is your train.”
Leo smiles warmly and says, “Thank you for your help.”
On Saturday morning, high school students gather in the park to volunteer for their local community.
Meeting the organizer, Leo waves with a warm smile and says, “We are glad to be here.”
He puts on sturdy work gloves and asks, “How can I help?”
Leo teams up with a partner and says, “Let's collect the bottles.”
They pick up discarded trash along the paths to recycle plastic containers properly.
Looking at the tidy walkways, the coordinator shouts, “Great teamwork everyone!”
Walking home with new friends, Leo feels proud of making his neighborhood a better place.
Leo looks out the window on a rainy morning.
He looks at the raindrops and says, “Look, it is raining!”
The weather is cold and wet today.
Leo runs to his room and says, “I need my jacket.”
Mom smiles and says, “Put on your boots.”
Mom points to the door and says, “Don't forget your umbrella.”
Leo takes his umbrella and smiles, ready to go outside.
After class on Friday, Kevin asks Amy, “What are you doing this weekend?”
Amy smiles and says that she has no special plans.
“Ethan and I want to ride a bicycle at the riverside park,” Kevin says.
He looks at Amy excitedly and asks, “Do you want to go with us?”
“Sounds like fun!” Amy replies with a big smile.
They agree to meet near the entrance, and Ethan checks the time on his phone.
Kevin waves happily to Amy and says, “See you on Saturday.”
On Sunday, my family walks happily into the zoo.
We are excited to visit every friendly animal.
We watch giraffes eat green leaves, and I say, “The giraffe is so tall.”
Then my little brother points and shouts, “Look at the elephant!”
Mom holds up her camera and asks, “Can we take a picture?”
We all smile together for the camera, and I say, “I love the zoo!”
